How do I argue against my assessed value?

Phone the Assessor on (417) 357-6145 and ask this year's Board of Equalization deadline. RSMo 138.060 tells the county board to decide valuation appeals in a summary way and adds that no presumption favors the assessor. Where a parcel's assessed value jumped by 15% or more over the previous assessment, other than through new construction or improvement, the assessor must show the figure is not above market value.

If you still owe the bill while arguing, RSMo 139.031 permits payment under protest. The full bill is paid before delinquency, a written statement of your reasons goes to the collector, and a circuit court action starts within 90 days. A taxpayer with a timely State Tax Commission appeal on file for that year skips the separate court action.

What if the bill goes past January 1?

Penalties and interest start running. RSMo 140.150 allows delinquent land to go to sale each August, on the fourth Monday. The collector writes to the owner of record before publication, and the owner may clear the tax, penalty, interest and costs any time ahead of the sale.

A seller who carries an open bill should plan to pay it from closing proceeds. Get the exact payoff from the Collector, since penalties change with the date, and pass that number to the title company. The Collector takes payment at its Galena office and in the courthouse drop box.

Is Stone County growing, and what do homes cost?

Population is rising. The Census Bureau's April 2020 base was 31,079 and the July 2025 estimate is 32,503, a gain of 4.6%. Over the same stretch St. Louis County and Stoddard County each lost 1.4%. Stone County belonged to the Branson micropolitan area until 2023, and the Branson West Municipal Airport sits two nautical miles west of the city of Branson West.

Density is 67.0 people per square mile on 463.83 square miles of land. Typical rent is $896, and owners report monthly costs of $1,451 with a mortgage and $476 without. About 88.1% of residents lived at the same address a year earlier. Among adults 25 and older, 91.8% finished high school and 24.8% finished a four-year degree or went further.

The Census lists 21,225 housing units for July 2025 and 13,530 households for 2020 to 2024, so the housing stock sits well above the count of households. When you set a price, compare your parcel with sales of similar houses in your own community and school district rather than leaning on the county's $249,000 figure.

It lies in southwest Missouri along the Arkansas line, bordered by Christian, Taney, Barry and Lawrence counties and by Carroll County, Arkansas. Galena is the seat and Kimberling City the largest city. Branson West, Reeds Spring, Crane, Hurley and Blue Eye round out the list of cities and villages, and part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside the county. Water covers 47 of its 511 square miles, or 9.2%.

The county counted 9,921 residents in 1970 and 31,076 in 2020. It was organized on February 10, 1851, and takes its name from William Stone, an early Maryland settler. The Census table adds the housing details.

Reeds Spring operates the most schools of those districts, with primary, elementary, intermediate, middle and high schools, and the Gibson Technical Center there offers vocational classes for grades 9 to 12. Libraries operate in Blue Eye, Crane, Galena and Kimberling City. Employment reached 5,681 in 2023, up 8.2% on 2022, and retail sales totaled $359,943,000 in 2022.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I find the Stone County Collector?

At 108 E. 4th Street in Galena, or by mail at P.O. Box 256, Galena, MO 65656. Call 417-357-6124. Courthouse hours run weekdays, eight to four.

Do they take credit cards for property tax?

Yes, in person, online, or through the number on your statement. The Collector lists a 2.4% fee with a $1.95 minimum, and no card numbers are given verbally by phone.

On what day does a Stone County bill become delinquent?

January 1. The bill is due by December 31, and mail needs a U.S. Post Office postmark of that date or earlier.

Which body decides the tax rate?

The taxing districts set it, usually by September 1. The county Assessor values property but has no part in rate setting, according to the county's own page.

What does selling in Bollinger County involve?

Commutes are long, with a mean travel time to work of 35.5 minutes compared with about 18 minutes in Boone or Buchanan County. On April 5, 2023, an EF2 tornado struck Glen Allen and Grassy and killed five people.

  • Building permits in 2025: 0

Applying the 19 percent residential rate listed by the Boone County Collector, a $179,800 house has an assessed value near $34,162. The 2020 census also found 17.1 percent of the 5,037 housing units vacant, a higher share than the 8.0 percent in Boone County or 11.4 percent in Buchanan County.

When are Bollinger County property taxes due?

Missouri sets the deadline at December 31 for every county, and Bollinger is no exception. State guidance says unpaid balances pick up interest and penalties after that day, and RSMo 139.100 treats a mailed payment as timely if the postmark falls inside the period. For bill timing, accepted payment types and the current mailing address, call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector.

For land that goes unpaid, RSMo 140.100 adds an 18 percent penalty on the year's delinquency, or at most 2 percent per month when redeemed before a sale. The tax sale falls on the fourth Monday in August, which was August 24 in 2026, and that date has passed.

How does the Bollinger County tax sale work?

RSMo 140.150 makes land with unpaid taxes or special assessments subject to sale on the fourth Monday in August each year. A few protections come with that.

  • The collector must mail a first class notice to the recorded owner before delinquent land is published for sale.
  • A second notice by certified mail is required when the assessed value is above $1,000.
  • If the certified notice comes back unsigned, a further first class notice goes to the owner and to any occupant.
  • Tax, penalty, interest and costs can be paid to the county collector at any time before the sale.

The statute also says that not receiving a notice does not cancel the tax. A seller who has moved should update the mailing address with the Collector's office, because notices go to the recorded owner.

Who is likely to buy a house in Bollinger County?

The buyer pool is small and local. The county is part of the Cape Girardeau metropolitan area, and Wikipedia describes its economy as resting mainly on agriculture and construction. 200 employer establishments and 1,396 jobs in 2023, down 2.9 percent from 2022, and retail sales of $8,970 per resident in 2022, far below the $23,978 recorded for Boone County. With a mean commute of 35.5 minutes, many residents work elsewhere in the region.

The 2020 census put the median age at 45.5 and found 4,177 households, 80.1 percent of them owner-occupied. Only 13.9 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 81.3 percent of households have a broadband subscription. Those facts point to long-term owners, family transfers and buyers who accept a long drive to work. For those buyers, a clean tax record and a prompt, well-documented closing are what keep a contract together.

How can a Bollinger County owner challenge an assessment?

Begin with the Assessor's office at 204 High Street, Suite 1. The Assessor values real and personal property each year, and the office can explain the factors used. Next comes the county Board of Equalization, where the filing deadline is the second Monday in July.

The state level is the Missouri State Tax Commission. Under RSMo 138.430 an owner may appeal the board's ruling within the time set by statute or 30 days after final action, whichever is later, and the Commission's guidance says the form can be filed online, by email or by mail to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102. An appeal for property owned by a corporation, LLC, trust or estate must come from an attorney.

An owner who wants to dispute value without missing the payment deadline can pay under protest. The State Tax Commission describes the steps as paying the whole bill by December 31, marking the check, and filing a written statement with the Collector that states the claimed market value.

What should a Bollinger County seller check before closing?

Treat the tax bill as part of the sale price discussion. Real estate tax follows the land, so a buyer takes the property subject to anything unpaid. A title company will normally order a tax search, and a seller can skip surprises by calling the Collector for the balance and asking whether any prior year is open.

If the Assessor holds the wrong mailing address, or the legal description on file differs from the deed, correct it before listing. The Recorder in Suite 7 keeps the deed record, and the Treasurer in Suite 8 is a separate office from the Collector. Ask each one for its own instructions rather than assuming the same counter handles them all.

Does Bollinger County have help for older homeowners?

With 22.8 percent of residents past 65, this question comes up often. The state Property Tax Credit program refunds up to $750 to qualifying older or disabled residents whose household income stays under set limits and who paid real estate tax or rent on their home. The Missouri Department of Revenue runs it, at 573-751-3505, and the claim goes on Form MO-PTC. Whether Bollinger County has adopted a local senior freeze is a question for the County Clerk at 573-238-1900.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Bollinger County property tax deadline?

December 31, the statewide deadline. Call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector to confirm how and where to pay.

Where is the Bollinger County Assessor?

At 204 High Street, Suite 1, Marble Hill, MO 63764. The main number is 573-238-1900, extension 1 for the Assessor.

When is the Bollinger County tax sale?

The fourth Monday in August under state law. That was August 24 in 2026, so the next one falls on the fourth Monday of August 2027.

Can unpaid taxes be paid before the sale?

Yes. RSMo 140.150 lets an owner pay the delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector at any time before the property is sold.

What is Bollinger County's population?

The Census Bureau estimates 10,646 for 2025, up 0.7 percent from the 2020 count of 10,567, spread across 618 square miles of land.

Where do I deal with property tax in Polk County, Missouri?

Everything is inside the Polk County Courthouse at 102 E Broadway in Bolivar, MO 65613. The Collector, Rachel Boyce, is in Suite 6 at (417) 326-4032. The Assessor, Rita Lemmon, is in Room 9, with the appraiser at (417) 326-4346 and personal property at (417) 326-4643. The County Clerk, Rachel Lightfoot, is in Suite 11 at (417) 326-4031.

The collector lists weekday hours of 8 to 4, although another line on the same page says 8 to 5, so call before a long drive. The assessor and clerk also list 8 to 4. The collector says its office handles more than $24 million a year for schools, roads, general revenue and other districts. See the Polk County Collector page.

What is Polk County like for someone selling a house?

Polk County lies in southwest Missouri and is part of the Springfield metropolitan area. It was split from Greene County on January 5, 1835, and named for Col. Ezekiel Polk. Bolivar is the seat, home to Southwest Baptist University and Bolivar Technical College, and the other cities are Fair Play, Humansville, Morrisville and Pleasant Hope. The assessor reports over 18,000 parcels of real estate and calls Polk a class three Missouri county.

The county between the low-cost and high-cost ends of the three counties in this guide set.

  • 33,604 residents in the 2025 estimate, 6.6 percent above April 2020.
  • 13,760 housing units, with owners living in 71.6 percent of occupied homes.
  • The middle owned home is worth $205,800, and the middle rent is $814.
  • Households earn a median $59,647, and 15.2 percent of residents are in poverty.
  • Workers travel 28.1 minutes to a job on average, the longest of the three counties.
  • The county issued 61 building permits in 2025.

Source: Census QuickFacts.

When does Polk County mail tax statements, and what is the penalty date?

Statements usually go out in the first part of November. If one does not arrive, ask the collector for a duplicate, since a missing bill does not cancel the tax. A payment postmarked after December 31 draws a penalty.

The office takes no partial payments on an amount due, and it cannot accept an incorrect figure. Personal property and real estate bills do not have to be paid together, but any delinquent tax has to be paid before the current year can be accepted. Online payment runs through a link on the collector's page, and paid-status lookups for real and personal accounts are listed there too.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Polk County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who owes the tax when a Polk County house changes hands?

The collector's page states that the current owner of real property is responsible for all taxes due on it, and that the law makes no provision for pro-rating a tax bill. Personal property is taxed on what you owned on January 1, so a vehicle sold in March still appears on that year's statement. The practical consequence for a seller is that the closing agent, not the county, divides the year between the two parties.

The collector also reminds owners that it is their duty to check that the parcel is described correctly and to give the assessor an updated mailing address. The collector has no authority to change a valuation without the assessor.

How does Polk County value real estate?

The assessor values everything as of January 1. Real property is reassessed in odd-numbered years, with new construction picked up every year. Rates are 19 percent of market value for residential, 32 percent for commercial and other, and 12 percent for agricultural property. Cars, trucks, boats and campers are assessed at 33.33 percent, farm equipment and livestock at 12 percent, and historic vehicles at 5 percent.

Increase notices are sent in the first week of June. Staff do exterior inspections only, carry photo identification and leave a card when nobody is home. State law bars them from entering the inside of a structure without permission. The assessor also notes that the levy is set by each taxing district, such as schools, fire, roads, cities, ambulance and hospitals, not by the assessor.

What is the path for disputing a Polk County assessment?

There are three levels, and the assessor's page gives dates for each.

Polk County appeal path from the county assessor's FAQ
LevelWhat to doDate given
Informal hearingCall (417) 326-4346 and meet an appraiserBefore June 30
Board of EqualizationGet the form from the County ClerkAppeal by the second Monday of July; hearings in the third week of July
State Tax CommissionFile online at stc.mo.govBy August 15, or thirty days after the board rules if that is later

The same page asks that the completed board form reach the Clerk before the second Wednesday in July, so ask the clerk at (417) 326-4031 which date controls. Skipping the board bars any later state appeal. Come with pictures, a recent sale or an appraisal, because changes require proof that the county's records are wrong. To pay under protest on a personal property dispute, tell the collector in writing and file with the State Tax Commission before December 31.

What happens at the Polk County delinquent land tax sale?

The sale is held on the fourth Monday in August at 10:00 a.m. at the courthouse, and the collector runs it. A parcel list is published in the Bolivar newspaper for three consecutive weeks beforehand. Owners may pay taxes, penalty, interest and costs at any time up to the sale. Bidding starts at the amount of taxes, penalties and sale costs, and buyers must be present and sign an affidavit that they owe no delinquent Missouri tax.

  • The buyer receives a Certificate of Purchase, held for one year or until redeemed.
  • The original owner may redeem within one year by paying the certificate amount plus 10 percent annual interest on the tax amount.
  • Later years' taxes paid by the buyer carry 8 percent annual interest.
  • Give the collector at least three business days' notice before redeeming, and allow about twenty minutes.

If the property is not redeemed, the certificate holder may seek a Collector's Deed after notices by certified mail at least ninety days ahead. The certificate becomes void if the requirements are not met by two years after the sale. A seller with a parcel on the list should call the collector before doing anything else.

Are there credits that lower a Polk County bill?

The assessor's page points to the state Property Tax Credit claim, Form 948, for people who may qualify for a credit or refund. The Missouri Department of Revenue describes the credit as covering qualifying seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals, up to $750 for renters and $1,100 for owners who occupy their home, based on tax or rent paid and household income (Missouri Department of Revenue).

For county-level programs beyond that, ask the County Clerk at (417) 326-4031 or the collector at (417) 326-4032.

Frequently asked questions

What is the penalty date for Polk County property tax?

A penalty applies to payments postmarked after December 31. Polk County bills are usually mailed in the first part of November.

Can I make a partial payment on a Polk County tax bill?

No. The Collector in Bolivar accepts no partial payments and will not take an incorrect amount. Real estate and personal property bills may be paid at different times, but delinquent years come first.

When is the Polk County tax sale?

It takes place on the fourth Monday in August at 10:00 a.m. at the Polk County Courthouse. Delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs can be paid to the Collector any time before the sale.

How long can I redeem a Polk County property sold for taxes?

The original owner has one year from the sale. Redemption costs the Certificate of Purchase amount plus 10 percent annual interest, plus 8 percent on any later taxes the buyer paid.

Where do I file a Polk County assessment appeal?

Start with the Assessor's appraiser at (417) 326-4346 before June 30, then use the County Clerk's Board of Equalization form. The State Tax Commission is the last step, by August 15 or thirty days after the board rules, whichever is later.

Who values and who bills property in Webster County?

In Webster County one office sets the value and another sends the bill. The Assessor sits in Room 19 of the Marshfield courthouse at 417-859-2169, and the Collector sits in Room 15 at 417-859-2683. Mail for the Collector goes to P.O. Box 288, Marshfield, MO 65706.

The Collector's site names Kevin Farr as the officeholder. It says the office brings in about $27 million of tax revenue each year, issues merchant licenses and conducts the delinquent tax sale every August. The counter stays open through lunch on weekdays until half past four.

The Assessor's page describes the task as putting fair market value on property as of the tax date. Two bodies can review that work: the county Board of Equalization and the Missouri State Tax Commission. The page links online personal property filing and a county GIS map. GIS access is a paid subscription arranged by phone.

Rates are a separate matter. Each taxing body adopts its own, and the county's Taxes page shows 2025 rates by school district.

When does a Webster County tax bill come due?

Webster County bills go out in November and are payable as soon as they arrive. December 31 is the cutoff. A check bearing that day's postmark or earlier is on time, while a later one is returned unless the late charges are enclosed.

Webster County Collector rules for the tax year, as posted on the Collector's site
TopicRule
StatementsMailed in November, due upon receipt
DeadlinePostmarked December 31 to avoid penalty and interest
Missing statementContact the office if none arrives by the end of November
Older yearsDelinquent years are paid before current taxes are accepted
Mail paymentsEnclose the bottom portion of the statement
In-person paymentsBring the statement
Delinquent tax saleHeld in August

Anyone paying late follows the schedule printed on the lower part of the statement. Under state law the postmark date is the payment date, and registered or certified mail uses its certification date instead.

How are Webster County homes valued for tax?

Missouri taxes residences on 19 percent of market value. Marshfield's own page repeats that figure along with 32 percent for commercial and industrial property, and says the county does the assessing and collecting for the city.

New real estate values are set in odd-numbered years and stay in place the following year except for new construction. That puts the next general reset on January 1, 2027. A planned increase above 15 percent on a house, improvements aside, calls for a visit to the property. Driving past does not meet the requirement, and the owner has no less than 30 days after the written notice to request an interior look.

  • Houses: 19 percent of true value.
  • Agricultural land: 12 percent.
  • Commercial and industrial: 32 percent.
  • Personal property: 33 and one-third percent, lower for livestock and farm machinery.

How do you contest a Webster County assessment?

Phone the Assessor at 417-859-2169 once a change notice lands, and ask how to set a hearing. The Board of Equalization comes first. Should the Board hold its number, the State Tax Commission is next, with a filing window of 30 days after the Board acts or the chapter's own date if that is later.

Payment need not wait. An owner who settles the entire current bill ahead of delinquency may give the Collector a written protest, and the disputed portion is parked in a separate account. That protest dies unless the owner sues the Collector in circuit court inside 90 days. A person with a timely Commission appeal pending skips the lawsuit, and a winning taxpayer receives the interest the fund earned.

The Assessor's page describes the State Tax Commission as the state agency with general supervision over assessors and the job of enforcing property tax law. The Assessor says it has no say over the budgets of the taxing bodies, so a high rate is a question for the school board, city or fire district rather than the Assessor's counter.

Is a senior tax freeze open in Webster County?

The 2026 application window for the senior citizens' property tax credit ran May 1 to June 30, 2026, so it has closed. Applicants had to be 62 before January 1, 2026, and the credit reaches residential real estate tax on a primary home. It holds the bill at 2026 base year levels. It is a freeze, and it does not exempt anything.

Two kinds of tax stay outside it: levies the state constitution guarantees, such as the blind fund and general obligation bonds, and voter-approved increases adopted after the base year. Vehicle tax and other personal property tax are excluded too. Forms were taken at the County Clerk's office in Room 12, with photo identification, a utility bill or voter card as proof of residency, and last year's paid receipt. The Clerk's line is 417-859-8683. Ask the Clerk when the next window opens, and what a mid-year sale does to an approved freeze.

What does the Marshfield city levy add to a bill?

Marshfield property owners pay the city's levy on top of the school, county and special district rates. After voters approve general obligation bonds, the Board of Aldermen sets a debt service rate high enough to cover principal and interest. The parks and cemetery levy has a ceiling that only voters can lift. That ceiling lets collections rise by 5 percent or the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower, against the prior year.

The county Taxes page breaks its 2025 rate tables into Diggins, Fordland, Marshfield, Niangua, Rogersville, Seymour and Strafford school districts, plus rural Webster County. Match the district printed on your statement, not the mailing city.

How do you pay a Webster County bill?

  • At the Collector's counter, with the statement in hand.
  • By mail, with the bottom portion of the statement enclosed.
  • On the Collector's website by e-check, debit or credit card, where cards add a convenience fee.
  • Accepted forms: cash, personal check, money order, cashier's check. One check can pay several bills.

The Collector says it is not responsible if you pay tax on property that belongs to someone else or skip a parcel you own, so check the account number against your parcel. A statement that never reached you does not erase the tax, penalty or interest.

What do Census figures say about Webster County households?

Webster County counted 36,202 people in the 2010 census and 39,085 in 2020. The 2020 to 2024 survey counts 13,964 households and finds 87.6 percent of residents in the same house a year before. The county is home to 2,990 veterans.

Owners occupy 77.4 percent of occupied homes, the lowest share of Stone, Warren and Webster, so renters have a larger presence here. Landlords get their statements in November like other owners and face the same December 31 postmark date.

The county is part of the Springfield metropolitan area. Six cities (Fordland, Marshfield, Niangua, Rogersville, Seymour and Strafford) and the village of Diggins make up its municipalities. Marshfield, at 1,490 feet, is the state's highest county seat, and its courthouse of Carthage marble dates from 1939 to 1941.

Frequently asked questions

When do Webster County property taxes become delinquent?

After December 31. Each statement is payable on arrival, and mail needs a postmark dated on or before the 31st.

Where is the Webster County Collector located?

Room 15 of the courthouse, 101 S. Crittenden Street, Marshfield. Mail goes to P.O. Box 288, and the phone is 417-859-2683.

Can I pay a Webster County bill by card?

Yes. The Collector's site takes cards, e-checks and debit, and card payments add a convenience fee.

Is the Webster County senior freeze accepting applications?

Not now. The 2026 window ended June 30, 2026. The County Clerk at 417-859-8683 can say when the next opens.

Who decides Webster County tax rates?

Each taxing body does, meaning schools, cities, fire districts and the county. The Assessor and Collector do not.
